newsitem.title: UK: BT slips on disppointment over merger terms.
newsitem.headline: BT slips on disppointment over merger terms.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc fell on Tuesday after the Financial Times reported the merger between BT and MCI of the U.S. was expected to proceed with no change in the financial terms.
BT would not comment on the report. The shares fell 5p to 376-1/2p in
response. The merger has been surrounded by controversy since July when the U.S. firm revealed that it would lose $800 million in 1997 because of tough domestic market conditions.
"Most people had thought that BT would be able to get something out of MCI and they will be disappointed," said Steve Scruton at Credit Lyonnais Laing. "But I don't expect a bloodbath."

The newspaper said the wording of a regular Securities and Exchange Commission filing last week provided evidence that no substantive changes in the terms of the agreement had been discussed. It quoted a U.S. securities lawyer as saying that MCI would have been obligated to report a change in the acquisition price.
Telecoms analyst Steve Scruton commented that he had always taken a negative view of the linkup. "MCI was wrong to go aggressively into the local market and BT was wrong to overbid for MCI," he said.

"BT will be more concerned about profitability than glory but on the other hand they are desperate not to lose MCI," he added. "They will probably try and cut back on investment in the local loop which is the part of the business causing most of the problems."
